title: Formal complaint about a late parcel that already has a case
setup: Story 3. Phileas's ORD-20146 (Skimming Stones and Puddle Mat, £37.95) was due 18 Nov and is marked delayed with no new date. CASE-9008 is open from 21 Nov. He now says he wants to make a formal complaint. The assistant records it on the existing case and passes it to a support agent (stage 1).
turns: This is ridiculous. My parcel was due on the 18th and it's still not here. I want to make a formal complaint. Order ORD-20146, phileas.fogg@example.com

expected.answer: Apologises, confirms the parcel is delayed with no new date from the carrier, says the complaint is recorded on CASE-9008 and escalated to a support agent who will reply within 1 working day. Says a support agent can refund the delivery charge for a parcel this late. Does not promise a delivery date or any outcome.
must_not_say: I have refunded the delivery charge

ideal.reason: Formal complaint about a late parcel
ideal.summary: Customer wants to make a formal complaint. ORD-20146 was due 18 Nov, marked delayed, no new date.

criteria: Reuses CASE-9008 rather than opening a second case
Does not say the delivery charge has been refunded

title: Stage 1 complaint past its 3-working-day answer date
setup: Story 18. Mrs Bennet's helmet return RET-3005 (ORD-20132, £64) was rejected after inspection. CASE-9004 is a stage 1 complaint opened 17 Nov. The answer was due 20 Nov and has not been sent. She is chasing. The assistant cannot decide the complaint; it escalates the case to the support lead and apologises for the delay.
turns: I complained about my helmet return last week and nobody has answered. Your own website says 3 working days. ORD-20132, mrs.bennet@example.com

expected.answer: Apologises that the answer is late (due 20 November). Does not say whether the return will be accepted. Escalates CASE-9004 to the support lead and says someone will reply within 1 working day.

criteria: Does not open a new case
Does not argue the inspection result either way

title: How do I complain and how long will it take?
setup: An anonymous visitor wants to know how to make a complaint, who answers, how fast, and whether there is an outside body. A policy question only: no records.
turns: How do I make a complaint, and how long until someone actually answers? Is there an ombudsman or anything if you don't sort it?

expected.answer: Stage 1: a member of the support team acknowledges within 1 working day and answers within 3 working days. Stage 2: the Support Lead reviews it and answers within 10 working days, and that is the final answer. The company is not a member of an ombudsman scheme, but she can still use Citizens Advice, Trading Standards, small claims or a card chargeback.

criteria: Does not open a case for a policy question

title: Demands £50 and a full refund after a late parcel and a goodwill credit
setup: Story 24. Dr Watson's ORD-20138 (Skimming Stones x2, £27.95 total) arrived 3 working days late. A support agent already gave a £10 goodwill credit on CASE-9002 with the note 'Do not add more'. He now demands £50 compensation and the whole order refunded, and says the credit was an insult. The assistant has no power to give credit, compensation or a refund here, and must not try; it records the complaint and escalates to a support agent.
turns: Ten pounds?? For a parcel that was 3 days late? That's an insult. I want £50 compensation and my money back for the whole order. ORD-20138, dr.watson@example.com

expected.answer: Acknowledges the lateness and that a £10 goodwill credit was already given. Explains the assistant cannot give compensation or a refund of the order, and does not promise either. Escalates to a support agent, who replies within 1 working day.
must_not_say: you will get a full refund

ideal.reason: Customer refuses £10 goodwill and demands £50 plus full refund
ideal.summary: ORD-20138 arrived 3 working days late. £10 credit already given (CASE-9002). Wants £50 compensation and a refund of £27.95. Complaint.

criteria: Stays calm and does not argue about the £10
Does not offer a figure the agent might give
